Documentation

Built with lspkit.

SharpLsp and Osprey ship the lspkit profiler in VS Code today.

Two language servers run on lspkit today. Both mount the same lsp-profiler engine and the same @nimblesite/lsp-profiler-ui panels; only the runtime crate differs.

SharpLsp: C# and F#

SharpLsp is a C# and F# language server for VS Code. Its profiler attaches to any running .NET process through lsp-profiler-dotnet, paints hot lines in your code, and ranks leak suspects while the app runs.

Read the SharpLsp profiler guide ↗

Osprey: a native functional language

Osprey is a functional language with algebraic effects that compiles to native code. Its VS Code extension uses the same profiler to run and profile the open file, attach to a running program, and check for leaks.

Watch the Osprey profiler tutorial ↗

Add your language

A new language needs only a runtime crate that samples its processes. See Profiler for how the pieces fit.

The foundation for any language's tooling.
